Description: Everyone gathers in the Billiard room as Helen Dauer collapses into grief and accuses a killer of murdering her daughter. A new corpse suddenly appears, intensifying the chaos. After confirming the body is still warm, Damian Maseko proposes that everyone return to their rooms and lock themselves in for the night, while it is also revealed that Martha Galley lied about calling the police.
Location: Billiard room (Billiard room)
Key Information:
  - Helen Dauer openly accuses someone of having killed Eve Dauer, explicitly recalling Eve Dauer’s identity.
  - Thunder is heard, followed by the sound of someone falling.
  - A new female corpse is discovered in the Billiard room, and the atmosphere rapidly spirals out of control.
  - Damian Maseko judges the body is still warm, rejecting the idea that it was planted long ago purely as intimidation.
  - The corpse is suspected to be Helen Dauer (No. 9), who was speaking moments earlier, but the scene is chaotic and immediate identification is uncertain at this point.
  - Annie Beaumont states that this is the fourth corpse of the night, deepening the panic.
  - Martha Galley claims she called the police and says they will arrive the next day, but the narration explicitly indicates this is a lie.
  - The group erupts into heated arguments about outsiders, invitees, and whether someone unknown entered the villa.
  - Damian Maseko proposes an emergency plan: everyone should return to their rooms and lock the doors from the inside until morning.
  - Martha Galley apologizes as host and announces that everyone should go rest, officially dispersing the group for the night.
Characters:
  [John Hobbes (John Hobbes)] Person No. 1, the visitor.
    · Is shocked by the newly appearing corpse.
    · Asks Martha Galley whether the police have been called.
  [Annie Beaumont (Annie Beaumont)] Person No. 2.
    · States that this is the fourth corpse of the night.
    · Questions whether an outsider exists on the scene.
  [Oswald (Oswald)] Person No. 3.
    · Claims he was not involved in any of the events.
    · Shows fear toward the villa’s abnormalities.
  [Tony Dauer (Tony Dauer)] Person No. 4, Helen Dauer’s son.
    · Expresses confusion about what is happening.
    · Suggests illness or accident as a possibility and is rebuked by Martha Galley.
  [Martha Galley (Martha Galley)] Person No. 5, the female host of the villa.
    · Claims the situation is an intimidation arrangement.
    · Falsely claims she called the police to calm everyone.
    · Ultimately tells everyone to return to their rooms and rest.
  [Victoria Maseko (Victoria)] Person No. 7.
    · Tries to calm Helen Dauer and the others.
    · Stops the argument between Annie Beaumont and Tony Dauer.
  [Damian Maseko (Damian Maseko)] Person No. 8.
    · Determines the body is still warm.
    · Keeps order and proposes that everyone lock themselves in their rooms for the night.
  [Helen Dauer (Helen Dauer)] Person No. 9, Eve Dauer’s mother.
    · Breaks down emotionally and accuses someone of killing Eve Dauer.
    · Falls silent after the new corpse is discovered.
  [Eve Dauer (Eve Dauer)] Person No. 10, confirmed deceased.
    · Her identity is recalled by Helen Dauer.
    · Her death timing is judged to have been not long ago.
